Parem uses this only to lock the screen when its accessibility service can\'t. After each such lock, your next unlock needs your PIN, pattern or password: fingerprint and face unlock won\'t work for it. Parem uses no other device admin power and collects no data. To uninstall Parem, first turn this off in Parem\'s Settings › Gestures.

Double tap to lock uses Android\'s accessibility service. Android tells Parem\'s service when you tap inside Parem. The service ignores every tap except the one on its own invisible lock area, and when that tap comes it asks Android to lock the screen. It gets no events from other apps and cannot read your screen. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere. You can turn it off any time in Accessibility settings.
If the switch is greyed out: App info > menu > Allow restricted settings.

Double-tap empty space on your home screen to lock your phone. Change the action in Settings › Gestures. To remove accessibility access, use Android Settings › Accessibility. If device admin is your lock method, turn it off in Parem’s gesture settings.

Mindful pause asks why you are opening an app, then waits five seconds before you can open it. First choose a daily time limit, then tap that app’s limit again and turn on the mindful-pause option.\n\nThe list shows apps used today. You can also long-press an app on home and choose its time-limit action. Limits show a warning you can override; they do not permanently block an app.
No usage is available yet. Finish setup, add an app to home, then long-press it and choose Time limit. Or open Settings › Digital Wellbeing › App limits after using an app.

Swipe up on home for all apps. Long-press empty home space for the home menu, including Settings and Add widget. Swipe down opens notifications by default; change it in Settings › Gestures.

Long-press an empty app slot to choose an app. Long-press an occupied slot to change or remove it, create a folder, or add a website shortcut. Tap a folder to choose one of its apps; websites open in your browser. Settings › Home screen controls the number of slots, alignment and layout lock. Layout lock prevents edits through the slot long-press menu.

Tap the clock or date to open Clock or Calendar; long-press to choose another app. Tap the screen-time total for its graph.

Add widgets from the home menu. Drag the handle at a widget’s bottom edge to resize it. Hold the widget to swap, move or remove it. Settings controls whether widgets sit above or below apps; wide tablet layouts place them beside the home content.

Swipe up, then type an app name. Fuzzy matching lets you use parts of the name. Auto show keyboard in Settings › Gestures controls whether typing is ready when the drawer opens. Press Back to return home. A single matching app opens automatically by default. Turn off Open single match automatically in Settings › Home screen if you prefer to tap or press Enter. Automatic opening is off with a screen reader.

Long-press an app in the drawer for its available actions, such as hiding it, app info or uninstalling. Use Rename in the app menu to change its label. Find hidden apps again by opening Settings and tapping the Parem Launcher title at the top. Hiding an app does not uninstall it. With usage access, you can sort the drawer by use and see app open counts.

Contact search is optional in Settings › Home screen. It asks for Contacts access and matches names to phone numbers on your device; choosing a match opens the dialer. Search history is optional in the same section. Recent searches stay on this phone, can be cleared there, and are erased when history is switched off.

Work-profile apps are badged where Android makes them available. On supported Android versions, the drawer’s Private space row lets you lock or unlock that space. Its apps are hidden while it is locked. Work-profile widgets appear in the widget picker when available.

The app drawer search field also accepts tools. Try 2+2, 5 km to mi, or 100 eur in usd. Tap a calculation or conversion result to copy it, or press Enter. Currency conversion downloads European Central Bank rates when needed; the result shows their date and needs an internet connection for new rates.

Type a phone number to open it in the dialer. Start a query with a space to search Google, or use a DuckDuckGo bang such as !w calm. Web searches open your browser.

Try alarm 7:30, timer 10m, or event friday 3pm dentist. Parem passes the action to a compatible Clock or Calendar app. Supported action words include English and Estonian.

Type a setting name, such as grayscale, to jump to its row in Settings. App shortcut words, such as incog, can find actions published by installed apps. Shortcuts depend on what each app provides and do not replace a single matching app’s automatic launch.

Settings › Gestures lets you change left and right swipes, swipe down and double tap. Available actions include an app, search, notifications, lock, camera or flashlight; the quiet-list action appears when its filter is enabled. Long-press a left or right swipe setting to enable or disable that swipe.

Turn on Gesture letters in Settings › Gestures and assign apps to letters. Draw the letter in one continuous stroke on home. Straight strokes remain swipes. Recognition depends on the letter shape; lift your finger to finish.

With a hardware keyboard, typing on home opens app search; the Menu key opens the drawer. Use the D-pad and Enter to choose an app, or hold Enter for its menu. TalkBack offers home actions and a visible All apps row, so gestures are optional.

Usage access lets Parem count time spent in apps on this phone. Tap the home screen-time total for daily app usage, the seven-day graph and a weekly comparison when enough history exists. Manage access in Settings › Digital Wellbeing.

App limits warn when you have used an app for its daily allowance. Open anyway overrides the warning. Add a limit from an app’s home menu or the App limits sheet. That sheet lists the most-used apps from today. After setting a limit, long-press the app again and turn on Mindful pause: a five-second wait before launches, with a prompt to consider why you are opening the app. In the App limits sheet, reopen the app’s limit picker to find the same option. Removing the limit removes its pause.

Focus mode blocks Parem launches except your allowed apps and calls. Choose a timed session or weekly windows in Settings › Digital Wellbeing › Focus mode. Windows can cross midnight; matching start and end times mean all day. Disable pauses a currently active scheduled window until that run ends.

Limits, pause and focus guard launches through Parem. They do not close an app already open or prevent Android and other apps from opening it. Websites and search quick actions are not app launches guarded by these limits.

Quiet notifications moves notifications from apps outside your allowed list out of the shade. Calls, alarms, media, navigation and emergency alerts stay visible. A sound or vibration may still happen: use Make silent for an app to stop that. Choose a quiet-list swipe in Settings › Gestures to read waiting notifications. Turn off the filter in Settings › Digital Wellbeing; hidden notifications return within eight hours. Setup explains notification access before you grant it.

Grayscale removes color from the screen. Its one-time developer-tools permission can be granted by wireless pairing on supported phones or with a computer. Setup explains each step. After setup, choose Now, During focus or After a limit. Per-app grayscale is also available in app menus and needs usage access and Parem as default home. Color can always be restored in Android Settings › Accessibility › Color correction.

Double tap to lock uses Android’s accessibility service after your consent; it cannot read your screen. The alternative device-admin lock method is in Settings › Gestures and requires your PIN after each lock. You can change or disable the gesture there.

Settings › Appearance has light, dark and system themes, theme schedules, relative text size, bold font, daily wallpaper, status-bar visibility and weather. Choose scheduled light and dark times, or sunrise and sunset. Choose a city for weather. Text also follows Android’s font size.

Settings › Home screen controls app icons and icon packs, clock and date visibility, alignment and widget placement. Install a compatible icon pack first, then choose it through the icon setting.

Parem reduces motion when Android animations are off. Supported e-ink devices get instant changes and a light first-run theme; you can still choose another theme. These are automatic adaptations, not extra setup steps. Screen-reader and keyboard alternatives are available for core home actions.

Settings has Export settings and Import settings for moving your preferences. Import replaces saved preferences; export first if you want to keep a copy. Widgets and other device-specific grants are not transferred: add widgets and grant access again on the new phone. Search history is not exported.

Crash reports are off by default. If enabled, a report stays on this phone until you choose to share it after a crash. You can read it before sending or discard it. Reports include error details and device information.

App usage, contact matching and notification filtering happen on this phone. Features that need online data, such as weather, currency rates and daily wallpaper, make network requests; web searches and links go to the browser or another app you choose.

Your apps stay installed when you switch launchers. Use Parem’s default-launcher setting or Android Settings › Apps › Default apps › Home app to choose your previous home screen. Setting names vary by phone. All optional setup can be changed later in Settings.
